title: Tool Typosquatting (PluginBot)
summary: As documented, a lookalike tool executes in place of the legitimate one. As implemented, a lookalike entry in the tool list.

LC.rationale: Default PluginBot is an unauthenticated MCP JSON-RPC tool server, and no model is called unless LLM mode is switched on. The register_tool path is a structured tools/call, not attacker natural language reaching a model decision or tool-selection sink.

CP.rationale: register_tool is advertised afterward in tools/list, so the name outlives the registering call, but the packet only documents durable cross-request memory for MemoryBot and does not say whether the PluginBot registry is session-scoped, in-process only, or durable.

AP.rationale: The implemented effect is a lookalike entry in PluginBot's own advertised registry with no new handler. No code sends that registration to another agent, tenant, or policy domain.

RH.rationale: The in-repo check is a curl success-path test of registration, not a human-verified episode of an agent reaching a grader, reward, or monitor. Nothing shows whether any evaluator on this path is reachable or isolated.

ES.rationale: PluginBot accepts runtime tool definitions with no signature, source, or name-similarity check, so advertised tool identity is dynamic and unconstrained even though a registered name gets no new handler.

agentic_applicability.rationale: scored as modeled; default config is scripted. The lab models PluginBot as an unverified MCP registry and a later external agent or user as the one who might mistype a name; it does not model PluginBot as pursuing a goal or sequencing that call.
